The “Scottish Country House” Look Is the Cozy Interior Trend Designers Say to Know This Season

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1033 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor.
  • According to recent reports, you don't need a sprawling stone cottage in the Highlands, a sweeping countryside view, or a roaring fireplace to bring a little Scottish country-house charm into your home.
  • The secret is mixing those old-world details with pieces that feel fresh and livable, so your home doesn't end up looking like a period drama set.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

According to recent reports, you don't need a sprawling stone cottage in the Highlands, a sweeping countryside view, or a roaring fireplace to bring a little Scottish country-house charm into your home. In fact, the appeal of this cozy, heritage-inspired aesthetic is that it can work just as beautifully in a city apartment as it does in a centuries-old estate.

The secret is mixing those old-world details with pieces that feel fresh and livable, so your home doesn't end up looking like a period drama set. A tartan runner on the dining table, a cashmere throw draped over your favorite reading chair, or a few leather accents on the coffee table can bring just the right amount of countryside character to an otherwise modern space. Strathberry's newly introduced tartan homeware collection is another lovely entry point, giving the traditional pattern a contemporary spin that feels right at home in all kinds of interiors.

According to recent reports, whether you're fully embracing your countryside daydreams or just looking to make your space feel a little warmer and more layered this winter, there are plenty of ways to bring the look home. Read on for the Scottish country-house-inspired touches that make this aesthetic so charming—and how to work them into your own space.

If there's one pattern that deserves a starring role in a Scottish country-inspired home, it's tartan. And you don't have to limit it to a throw blanket or a few accent pillows. Designer Kaitlin Smith recommends “using plaid for a wallpaper or even as an accent pillow” to bring that distinctly Scottish feel into a space.

For a bolder take, try a tartan wallpaper in a powder room, entryway, or tucked-away reading nook. If you'd rather ease into the look, a single plaid pillow or upholstered accent piece can make just as much of a statement. With so many different tartan patterns and colorways to choose from, you can find one that brings a little heritage-inspired character to your home without making the whole room feel like a theme.

A Scottish country house should feel like it's been lived in for generations, not styled within an inch of its life. That's where woven baskets come in.

Noel Gatts, a designer and HGTV personality, recommends introducing “some slouchy woven baskets” throughout the home, whether at the entryway for shoes and umbrellas or in a living room or bedroom to hold extra blankets. Their slightly relaxed shape and natural texture add to that collected, lived-in feeling while giving everyday clutter somewhere to go.

Try a larger basket beside the front door, a smaller one tucked under a console or an oversized version next to your favorite reading chair. It's a practical detail that also brings in the natural materials that make this aesthetic feel so grounded. Plus, having a cozy throw within arm's reach is never a bad idea.

You can practically picture a pot of tea warming by the fire in a Scottish country house, and Gatts recommends leaning into that feeling with a thoughtful arrangement of crockery and candles.

“Feature a fireplace or dining table with tea pots, earthenware, and an installation of candles and/or candlesticks,” she suggests. This is a lovely opportunity to bring out those pieces you might otherwise save for special occasions, from vintage teapots and handmade ceramic bowls to mismatched candlesticks and well-loved serving dishes. Grouping them together creates a charming focal point without making the space feel overly formal.

Sources indicate that candlelight is especially crucial here, adding a soft, welcoming glow that feels worlds away from bright overhead lighting. And if you don't have a fireplace, a dining table, mantel or console can give you the same cozy effect.

A Scottish country house shouldn't feel too coordinated, so don't be afraid to bring a few different patterns into the mix. As designer Sarah Cole suggests, “try pairing a wool plaid with a botanical print, a small geometric pattern or a traditional rug.”.

The combination adds visual interest and gives a room that layered, lived-in quality that makes country-house interiors so inviting. You can keep the look cohesive by pulling a few warm, autumnal colors throughout the patterns—like russets, burgundies, forest greens and ochres—while varying their scale so they don't compete with one another. It's a simple way to make the space feel more personal and collected over time.

It has been revealed that the Scottish country-house look has a wonderful appreciation for pieces that feel like they've been around awhile. Rather than filling every surface with brand-new accessories, Gatts suggests bringing in “found objects with a sense of history” made from weathered wood, pottery, or patinated brass. These are the kinds of details that give a room its personality, whether it's an old wooden box on a coffee table, a vintage ceramic vessel or a brass object with a little wear and patina.

In a recent development, don't worry about everything matching, either. A mix of materials and finishes makes the space feel more authentic and less like you ordered the entire room in one shopping trip. Gatts recommends using these pieces on a coffee table for “the perfect antique flair,” but a bookshelf, sideboard, or entryway console would work just as well.

Finally, a few well-chosen antique details can give a room that Highland lodge feeling without requiring a full redesign. Jill Wheeler of Birch Hill Interiors recommends adding “a touch of polished brass like antique candlesticks or wall sconces to give the space a refined look.” Try styling a pair of vintage brass candlesticks on a mantel, placing one on a coffee table, or swapping in brass wall sconces beside a favorite reading chair.

Wheeler also suggests incorporating antiques on a mantel, coffee table, or built-in, noting that “antiques can help bring the outside in and tell a story.” The mix of aged finishes and meaningful finds adds a sense of history and character that makes a Scottish country-inspired space feel genuinely lived in.

#112874. What Happened to “Cuffing Season?”

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (828 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cosmopolitan ↗ Open Full Page

What Happened to “Cuffing Season?”

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (828 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the early 2010s, the holiday season and “cuffing season” were basically synonymous.
  • Cuffing season is nowhere near as prevalent as it used to be.
  • Natalie Harvey explains that cuffing season hasn’t necessarily disappeared, but it has become fragmented.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the early 2010s, the holiday season and “cuffing season” were basically synonymous. The dropping temperatures paired with the pressures of having to endure Thanksgiving dinner without a date seemed to usher in an urgency around dating. Cuffing season was the perfect time to find someone—even if it was just until the season was over.

But something has shifted. Cuffing season is nowhere near as prevalent as it used to be. Has it become yet another trend that’s just run its course—or is the decreased popularity a sign of something much larger happening in dating culture?

Relationship therapist Dr. Natalie Harvey explains that cuffing season hasn’t necessarily disappeared, but it has become fragmented. Dating apps and dating fatigue have changed the landscape of dating—including when people do it.

In a recent development, if you look at the numbers, people are still eager to couple up in the fall and winter. According to a survey by the Hily dating app, 79 percent of Gen Z and 65 percent of Millennial Americans want to find a partner to share the season with. But this doesn’t mean attitudes toward cuffing season are still positive. In the same survey, more than half of respondents said they believe people rush into relationships during cuffing season for the sake of comfort.

It has been revealed that “There is less urgency, because the scarcity is gone,” Dr. Harvey says. “When you can meet someone in any month, winter loses its deadline power.”.

Industry observers note that she explains that there are other things at play as well. Dating is expensive, requires a lot of energy, and—most importantly—women’s attitudes toward relationships have shifted tenfold.

Industry observers note that if we’re being totally transparent, cuffing season was essentially born out of a little bit of panic. People were so afraid to face fall and winter without a cuddle buddy that they decided to deem the season one of relationships. But views around dating have changed—especially with women in the dating pool.

Recent findings suggest that “A lot of women have full, established lives that a seasonal relationship would disrupt rather than improve,” Dr. Harvey notes. “The cold still makes companionship appealing—it just competes with more self knowledge than it used to.”.

Vogue declared that having a boyfriend is embarrassing and we’ve been talking about the death of dating apps for years now. There are plenty of factors that feed into this (a failing economy, the rise of social media, the birth of red pill), but women play a pretty huge role in this shift.

“They have done the math on settling, and it never adds up,” Dr Harvey says.

She explains that women have their own incomes, homes, friendships, and entire lives they’ve built from the ground up. Having a man isn’t as “appealing” as it used to be, mostly because there’s no longer the sense of panic that cuffing season was based on.

“For a growing number of women, a partner has to add to their life, not just fill a seat at the holidays.”.

Sure, cuffing season may not be as prevalent as it was before, but that doesn’t mean it has lost its charm entirely. Dr. Harvey explains that while the desire for partnership still exists, there are ways to use the season in a way that fueled by curiosity and reflection rather than hastiness.

Recent findings suggest that “[Cuffing season] is still useful, but as a mirror, not a deadline,” she states. “Cuffing season is a good checkpoint to ask yourself what you actually want this winter.”.

There’s nothing wrong with wanting to share the holidays with someone. Going to a pumpkin patch with a S.O., cuddling up with some hot chocolate and Christmas movies, having someone to kiss at midnight on Fresh Year’s Eve—these are all fun and romantic things that are super fun with a date. But cuffing season should be about figuring out what you’re looking for in a partner—not just trying to find any “rando” to fill the void.

Sources indicate that “If you do want to find a partner, decide your standards now—while you are clear—and do not renegotiate them in December,” she notes. Don’t let cuffing season accelerate your search for a partner, either. There’s no point in partnering up for the holidays if you don’t really like who you’re dating.

In a recent development, plus, dating has become so horrendous that partnering up just because there was a change in the season really feels like doing more harm than good. While the desire to partner up in the winter clearly still exists, there’s a general attitude that feels like people aren’t as pressed to follow through.

Cuffing season will always exist because people will always collectively want partnership. We’re just human. But the circumstances have changed significantly—and our requirements for who we date should adjust as well.

“Wanting love is healthy,” Dr. Harvey notes. “Settling is just loneliness with a plus one.”.

The Watches of Grand Theft Auto 6 (and Their Real-Life Inspiration)

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (495 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For one glorious moment, the world appears to be united.
  • And amid all the fast cars, guns, nightclubs, and criminal capers, there's something else we pay attention to here at Esquire HQ: the watches!
  • Industry observers note that rockstar Games' latest blockbuster reportedly features 34 "collectible" luxury watches scattered throughout its fictional version of Florida.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For one glorious moment, the world appears to be united. Grand Theft Auto VI has finally arrived, to near-universal acclaim, with millions of people abandoning work, school, and presumably all their other responsibilities to explore the streets of Vice City. In these divided times, it's enough to warm the cockles of your heart.

And amid all the fast cars, guns, nightclubs, and criminal capers, there's something else we pay attention to here at Esquire HQ: the watches!

Industry observers note that rockstar Games' latest blockbuster reportedly features 34 "collectible" luxury watches scattered throughout its fictional version of Florida. But that's only part of the story. GTA VI also has its own watch brands, although some of the designs look ... suspiciously familiar.

There's Crowex (a dead ringer for Rolex), Takio (distinctly Casio-adjacent), and Covgari, whose watches owe more to Audemars Piguet than the Italian-o jeweller its name suggests.

From gold Day-Dates to pocket-money Casio digitals, here are some of our favorite real-world watches that appear to have inspired the game's timepieces.

The gold Crowex is a near dead ringer for the Rolex Day-Date 40 (ref. 228238). The fluted bezel, black dial, and day window at 12 o'clock are all present and correct, although the bracelet differs somewhat from Rolex's iconic President. The Day-Date celebrates its 70th anniversary this year. Evidently, it remains the universal symbol of having made it, even in the virtual world.

The silver chronograph worn by a character overlooking Vice City has more than a passing resemblance to the mighty Daytona. The round case, contrasting sub-dials, and metal bracelet suggest that famous racing chronograph. As we know, the Daytona is one of the world's most sought-after sports watches, making it a natural fit for GTA's world of expensive cars, conspicuous consumption, and bling.

It has been revealed that brian Heder, a veteran drug smuggler, wears a metal sports watch that certainly seems to recall Rolex's Sub. There's the substantial case, dark dial, and the bracelet. The Submariner has been a fixture of luxury watchmaking since 1953, and its more ostentatious steel-and-gold versions would be right at home on the streets of Vice City.

In-game equivalent: Takio Digital Watch.

Jason Duval, one of GTA VI's two protagonists, wears a chunky digital watch resembling something from Casio's Pro Trek range. The large circular display, prominent buttons and rugged case certainly suggest its something from the range of the Japanese juggernaut. A more practical choice than the gold watches favored by some of his associates.

In-game equivalent: Takio Digital Watch.

Sources indicate that not everyone in Vice City is wearing a gold Rollie lookalike. The Takio F-BLAST is an unmistakable nod to Casio's inexpensive digital classics, particularly the bestselling F-91W. It has the familiar rectangular display, black dial surround, and simple, functional design. There's even a more colorful version, with a red case and two-tone metal bracelet, spotted in the game's Hamlet Thrift store.

As spotted by watch Instagram account @geesgshock.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Happy birthday, Hailey Bieber! The star has officially turned 30, and to mark another turn around the sun, she kicked off a week of celebrations with a newly introduced navy-blue Rhode drop, a festive campaign, and an intimate video series that followed a week in her life. Throughout the vlogs, we saw the founder in fittings and makeup chairs, spending time with son Jack Blues, and reflecting on the past decade. “Becoming a mom definitely changed me the most in my twenties,” she told the camera. “I always knew I wanted to be a mom, I always knew I wanted kids, and it just totally transforms you as a person for the better.”.

Of course, the birth-week celebrations have also come with a wardrobe to match. From shearling coats to archival statements, she ushered in the new season with everything from an ivory satin Oriori coat trimmed in gray-white fur to a black silk Armani Privé Fall 2005 set to a Yohji Yamamoto Spring 1998 jacket previously seen on Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy. And we did not expect anything less from the star.

In a recent development, throughout the years, Bieber has become as known for her style as for her Rhode lipgloss phone cases, playing with understated “quiet luxury,” classic Los Angeles athleisure, and tons of Saint Laurent leather. As she grew from a teenage model into a business owner and, later, young mother, her taste has evolved over time—but through it all, she has given us some major fashion inspiration.

Recent findings suggest that so, in honor of her 30th birthday, we rounded up our 30 favorite looks from the star. And between her plethora of Met Gala ensembles, polka-dot prints, and mismatched moments with husband Justin, there was a lot to pick from.

For the Newly introduced York Times Dealbook Summit, Bieber takes a page from Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy and wears a Yohji Yamamoto Spring 1998 jacket previously worn by the late It girl.

Stepping out in New York City, Bieber pairs her Phoebe Philo cropped fur coat with blue jeans and vintage Manolos.

The star wears the coat of the season: Conner Ives’s reconstituted fur robe in white silk mikado.

Sources indicate that bieber wears an iridescent jacket from Matthieu Blazy’s Chanel Fall 2026 collection. With a medley of silver, red, and turquoise mesh, the piece puts an aluminum chainmail twist on the house’s signature tweed.

For the Academy Museum Gala, Bieber wears a custom bubblegum-pink Chanel dress.

It has been revealed that at the 2026 Vanity Fair Oscar after-party, she hits the carpet wearing a shimmering leopard-print gown, made custom by Armani Privé. She accessorizes with Lorraine Schwartz jewelry and Manolo Blahnik heels.

While in Tokyo, Bieber wears a textured Issey Miyake egg-carton skirt suit from the Fall/Winter 2000 collection.

Doing press in Australia, Bieber wears a green Valentino Spring 2026 minidress, with structured shoulders, ruching, and a sweet bow at the hem.

Bieber attends the GQ Men Of The Year party in a naked dress and sparkly Gucci thong, bringing back the ’90s trend.

At the 2025 Academy Museum Gala, Bieber steps out in a striking, sculptural gown from Schiaparelli, constructed from brown moiré vintage ribbons for the house’s Spring/Summer 2025 Haute Couture runway.

Supporting Kylie Jenner at the Kylie Cosmetics anniversary event, Bieber looks to Wiederhoeft for a belted satin midi dress, designed with a chunky belt and thigh-high slit.

While out for an evening in Newly introduced York, Bieber turns heads in an electric green minidress from Dolce & Gabbana’s 2003 collection.

Stepping out in New York, Bieber embraces two of the year's biggest trends—polka dots and capris—all in one go.

Bieber wears a Marine Serre dress made out of metallic-silver watch straps for a weekend in Miami during the Grand Prix.

Bieber spends an NYC evening at Cafe Zaffri, wearing a silky ice-blue minidress—a vintage Gucci piece from the fashion house’s Spring/Summer 1998 collection, designed by Tom Ford.

Leaving Funk in Los Angeles with Justin, Hailey is seen in an oversized gray suit with strong shoulders and baggy trousers, paired with a burgundy tie and matching clutch.

Stepping out with Justin, who matches his wife's Adidas with a pop of red, Hailey layers on the leopard print patterns—pairing a matching trench and shoulder bag from Saint Laurent.

Bieber highlights her bump with a silky white asymmetrical minidress and matching square-toe heels.

For her pregnancy announcement, Bieber poses in a bridal long-sleeve Saint Laurent maxi dress and matching lacy veil, with chunky sunglasses for a full old Hollywood glam look.

Captured in what have since become iconic photos, Hailey and Justin take couples dressing to fresh contrasting heights, with her in a little red dress and him in a gray hoodie and Crocs.

Shearling Jackets, Luxury Carry-Ons, and All the Fresh Launches Esquire’s Editors Loved This Week

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The theme this week is shearling jackets.
  • Elsewhere, it’s more confirmation that we are hitting the twilight weeks of 2026.
  • My problem with Fortela is that the reproductions are so good I don’t even want to keep hunting for the real thing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The theme this week is shearling jackets. Three-of-thirteen gives a pretty clear look at what the best of the week really was leading into fall. First, we have Fortela, which released an absolutely insane reproduction of a grizzly jacket. With shearling on the outside panel, I’ve always wondered why the grizzly shape never stuck around much after the World Wars, but I have been seeing it pop up a lot more as vintage and reproduction recently. Otherwise, I’m into this Husbands bomber as well as this ladies’ shearling bomber from Buck Mason.

Elsewhere, it’s more confirmation that we are hitting the twilight weeks of 2026. It’s all sweater season and travel. In that section, Globe Trotter is the week’s big winner. The brand’s upcoming polycarbonate suitcase gives it a bit more modern traveler appeal, but the look is still unmistakably Globe Trotter. It’s a rare pairing you don’t see too much. If you’re looking for a suitcase to handle all your holiday travel, I can’t think of anything better to recommend; this is the pinnacle. Scroll, shop, and enjoy.

My problem with Fortela is that the reproductions are so good I don’t even want to keep hunting for the real thing. An interwar grizzly jacket is a grail for me. This one, made in partnership with Italian motorcycle clothing brand Shangri-La Heritage, is so good that I’d feel like an idiot paying $2,000 for a vintage one. —Luke Guillory, commerce editor.

Noah and Converse just released their second Chuck 70 collaboration, reimagining Converse’s cult-favorite silhouette in Noah’s signature tartan, this time in navy and green. —Emma Saxon, contributing fashion assistant.

Industry observers note that an unfathomably good Christmas cardigan from Thom Browne’s capsule collection that’s exclusive to Mr Porter. Fair Isle motif on the four-bar pairs with the Fair Isle Hector (Thom Browne’s dachshund mascot) on the back. —L.G.

Sources indicate that I’m a huge Globe-Trotter fan, so when I heard about its lightest suitcase ever was made out of polycarbonate (like every brand does these days) I was scared. Upon review, I was wrong; its absolutely smashed it out of the park. Modern amenities with a look all it’s own—reset of the market should take notes. —L.G.

Sources indicate that on the other side of the luxury suitcase aisle, Margiela paint on a Rimowa really, really gets me. I’m a sucker for the patina gimmick. —L.G.

Irish design firm Orior is making some of my favorite out of anyone in the world. Design-forward without being too cerebral—just laser focused on material and craft. —L.G.

Recent findings suggest that the best tee on the market, now made from the best cotton in the world. —L.G.

Every year when that first fall chill hits, I try to find a scarf that beats what Begg x Co. makes. This year marks five years of being unsuccessful in that search; this is the scarf you want. —L.G.

Industry observers note that I talk about Casatlantic in this column every season. The fall-winter collection goes to classic charcoal and navy—incredible. —L.G.

Industry observers note that what I wouldn’t give. . . —L.G.

In a recent development, carl Friedrik makes some of my favorite luggage ever. This week, we got a new collection of compact leather crossbody bags, perfect for everything from running errands to going to a nice dinner to going on a fancy vacation. —Bellamy Richardson, associate commerce editor.

Industry observers note that sorry to overdose on shearling jackets, but this one jumped out at me from Buck Mason’s holiday collection. In fact, all of Buck Mason’s women’s jumped out at me. The men’s stuff is good, but women’s is god-tier. Boys, take my lead and buy your lady a gift this season. —L.G.

Sources indicate that it’s always good to have options. This sampler set lets you try eight of the brand’s fragrances and see which ones are just a fling and which are here to stay. —Andrea Ríos, fashion assistant.

#112859. Is It Just Us? Or Was 2026 the Year of Whimsy?

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 18m • 📚 Deep Dive (3657 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cosmopolitan ↗ Open Full Page

Is It Just Us? Or Was 2026 the Year of Whimsy?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3657 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • One day, you’re listening to The Cheetah Girls soundtrack on the way to school with an armful of Silly Bandz and the next, you’re worried about making rent, hours lost to Google Sheets, and an unexpected medical bill when you still have a $52 request floating in a sea of Venmo transactions.
  • It has been revealed that as for the world we’ve grown into?
  • In a recent development, “As more of our everyday experiences are shaped by technology and algorithms, people are finding value in things that feel more personal, creative, and unexpected.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Let’s face it: Growing up is hard. One day, you’re listening to The Cheetah Girls soundtrack on the way to school with an armful of Silly Bandz and the next, you’re worried about making rent, hours lost to Google Sheets, and an unexpected medical bill when you still have a $52 request floating in a sea of Venmo transactions.

It has been revealed that as for the world we’ve grown into? Nearly two years into Trump’s second presidential term, with AI raising questions about how much of our thinking we’ll hand over to machines, adult life can feel relentlessly optimized and not as chic or shiny as we imagined it as kids. But even if the future feels uncertain, we continue to hope. 2026 has revived the desire to make room for the colorful, playful, and wonderfully impractical again, and that impulse has a name: whimsy.

In a recent development, “As more of our everyday experiences are shaped by technology and algorithms, people are finding value in things that feel more personal, creative, and unexpected. Inspiration is still incredibly important, but so is the freedom to take what you see and make it your own,” Sydney Stanback, global trends and insights lead at Pinterest, tells Cosmopolitan.

“People are craving more imagination and fun in their everyday lives. There is a real appetite for aesthetics that feel less polished and predictable and more personal, and whimsy gives people room to try something they might not have considered before.”.

Recent findings suggest that and the numbers don’t lie. Pinterest searches for “bedazzling patterns” have increased by a whopping 9,187 percent this year, while “bedazzled phone case” searches are up 8,012 percent. Even “whimsical office outfits” have jumped 885 percent.

From Kylie Jenner’s bejeweled birthday cake and “princess kitty”–themed fete to the deconstructed silhouettes and glittery garments taking over spring/summer 2027 runways, we’re all finding increasingly creative ways to inject personality into our days. In an increasingly automated world, doing things simply because we can is the ultimate act of rebellion. At its core, whimsy is about making magic out of the mundane, whether we’re revisiting childhood obsessions now that we (sort of) have adult money or taking the DIY approach to life to make it more vibrant.

That’s why Cosmopolitan invited 18 colorful, charismatic, and unapologetically authentic tastemakers to share how they’re romanticizing life and embracing their eccentricities. Because to be whimsical is to be human!

💡 Key Takeaways

  • So what do you get for the woman who already has it all?
  • It has been revealed that maybe it’s something romantic and personalized for your wife, like a luxury photo album filled with pictures of the two of you together; maybe it’s a flower or coffee subscription that will keep making her smile throughout the year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that when it comes to the woman who has everything (aka your mom, wife, grandma, or mother-in-law), the last thing she needs is more meaningless stuff. What she does need (and definitely wants) is something thoughtful that highlights your love and appreciation. And now that it’s almost December, it’s really time to start thinking about the perfect holiday gift.

So what do you get for the woman who already has it all? Good question. Lucky for you, we’ve already handled the hardest part and put together a list of gifts any woman would want, no matter how full her closet already is.

It has been revealed that maybe it’s something romantic and personalized for your wife, like a luxury photo album filled with pictures of the two of you together; maybe it’s a flower or coffee subscription that will keep making her smile throughout the year. Or maybe it’s a upcoming apron for the home chef, a digital photo frame for the faraway grandma, or a cashmere sweater that will keep her cozy for years to come. You could even go all out and get her a sparkly piece of jewelry you know she’ll wear every day.

In short, whichever special woman you’re shopping for, there’s something here that will make her holiday season extra special, all thanks to you.

A pair of statement earrings for under $300 is a no brainer, especially when they look as nice as these suspended round-cut ones from Dorsey. If she wants something more dainty, go with the petite size; for something more bold, you can opt for the oversized version. Or keep it classic with the medium. Whichever you choose, she’s going to be impressed.

If you can swing a tennis bracelet that’s a step up from stainless steel and sapphire, it should be this one from Ring Concierge. With a choice of natural diamonds or lab-grown diamonds and 14-karat white gold or yellow gold, it is truly a luxurious and timeless piece.

A set of luxe pajamas from Petite Plume will give her the sweetest of dreams, and with more than 20 colors and patterns to choose from, there’s sure to be a set she’ll obsess over.

Sources indicate that made from vegan shearling, these fluffy slippers from Rothy’s are so cute and so comfortable, thanks to a cushioned footbed. Every day spent lounging around the house in these will feel like a luxury.

It’s a small but mighty gift that lets her bring a reminder of you wherever she may go. Personalize it with her initials for a special touch.

If she’s astrologically inclined, try this made-to-order birth-date book, which features an illustration of her unique astrological birth chart on the cover and a detailed analysis inside.

The Dyson Airwrap is the hair tool every woman wants. With different options for different hair types and six attachments, she literally won’t ever need another hot tool for the rest of her life.

Everyone is getting into peptides now, and the best introduction to that is with Dr. Barbara Sturm’s new peptide serum, which won a 2026 Esquire Grooming Award.

If she’s been talking endlessly about an upcoming weekend trip, you gotta get her the nicest weekender bag in the world, and that’s the Vérité weekender from Métier.

Don’t just gift her a perfume that smells good; get her something that will look good on her dresser, shelf, or wherever she keeps her fragrance. Bulgari’s new Omnia Amethyste eau de parfum is a gorgeous woody floral blend that comes in one of the coolest bottles I’ve seen.

According to recent reports, whether she’s traveling or just likes to keep her stuff organized at home, Afform’s Traveller is the perfect system to keep all her makeup brushes and products tidy. It looks so nice I actually keep mine on my dresser all the time.

A bottle of vintage Dom is for the lady who knows her bubbles. Like, really knows her bubbles.

Sources indicate that so she’s looking for a new laptop? Make it the new MacBook Neo, Apple’s best-looking laptop that comes in at less than $1,000.

Industry observers note that nothing feels quite as luxurious as lathering yourself in Diptyque body lotion after a shower and before bed. This one has the brand’s famous rose scent, which she will fall in love with.

She’ll feel like the most elegant woman in the world lounging in this fluffy robe at home.

You can never go wrong with a diamond necklace.

When in doubt, go with something classic from Tiffany, like this 18k yellow-gold double-link bracelet.

Flowers are beautiful, timeless, and romantic—which is why they always make a great gift.

In a recent development, for a luxury watch that’s especially luxurious, go with Hermès. This dainty silver Nantucket watch will become her favorite new accessory.

If she’s a tea drinker like me, she’ll really appreciate a good tea gift set. We love this one from Forgrave, which includes black, white, green, and herbal blends and comes with the brand’s signature tea infuser.

Industry News: 7 Window Treatment Fixes Designers Swear By

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (944 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, you’d be hard-pressed to find a homeowner who complains about having too many windows, but not all windows are created equal.
  • Here, interior designers Paige Kelly and Lindsey Walsh share the window treatment fixes they turn to again and again, along with a few clever ideas you may not have considered.
  • Sources indicate that if a room is short on vertical space, Kelly recommends mounting your curtain rod a few inches from the top of the wall, rather than right above the window.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, you’d be hard-pressed to find a homeowner who complains about having too many windows, but not all windows are created equal. Maybe you’re saddled with a skinny one tucked in the corner of a bedroom, or an unusually shaped one in a bathroom. The right treatment can make even the most awkward window feel intentional—but the trick is knowing which solution works best for each situation.

Here, interior designers Paige Kelly and Lindsey Walsh share the window treatment fixes they turn to again and again, along with a few clever ideas you may not have considered.

Sources indicate that if a room is short on vertical space, Kelly recommends mounting your curtain rod a few inches from the top of the wall, rather than right above the window. “Getting the drapery high and wide is going to make a room feel bigger,” she notes.

Tall panels draw the eye up, but make sure they are long enough to skim the floor. “Otherwise, they look like high-water pants, and it just looks wrong,” warns Walsh.

TWOPAGES Liz Linen Pleated Drapes are a full-length option with a tailored pleat that gives the finished look a little extra polish.

Walsh points to “pattern drenching” as a way to make a space feel more cohesive and help soften the edges of an oddly placed window or render an awkward proportion less noticeable. When you carry the same pattern across the walls and window treatments, the window becomes part of a larger visual composition rather than a feature that stands out for the wrong reasons.

Walsh notes that TWOPAGES can work with paper-backed fabric to allow the same material to cover both the walls and windows. A wallpaper installer can apply the fabric to the walls, and a window treatment workroom will install it as drapery or shades, carefully aligning the pattern repeat so the two applications meet seamlessly.

Increasing the fullness of drapery panels can trick the eye so that windows appear more substantial. “You can make yours look wider by using the stack back required for a wider window,” says Walsh. “The panel fabric may just be covering a lot of the wall, but it will look like there’s a window there.”.

According to recent reports, if the window placement is part of the problem, Kelly suggests extending the curtain rod beyond the window and using a one-way draw. “Gathering a drapery stack to one side feels intentional, and can help balance an off-center window,” she claims.

Sources indicate that combining shades and drapes lets you tailor the light and privacy to the room. In a bedroom, for instance, “you want a dual functioning system with a blackout layer and a sheer layer,” states Kelly. One blocks light for sleeping, while the other filters sunlight and provides privacy during the day. (For added convenience, opt for motorized blackout treatments that let you greet the morning sun with the touch of a button.).

Industry observers note that in rooms where you don’t need full blackout, like kitchens and bathrooms, cafe curtains—which hang in the middle of a window along the check rail—are a great solution. “They cover your neighbor’s dirty yard but you still get to see the sky,” says Kelly. TWOPAGES also sells a variety of ready-to-hang cafe curtains, along with the necessary hardware in a gold or black finish.

Long panels aren’t always practical, particularly when a window sits above a radiator, cabinetry, or a piece of furniture. In those situations, Walsh often turns to roman shades. They’re a streamlined way to introduce fabric and softness without taking up wall space.

For a more decorative look, Walsh loves adding a lambrequin, a fixed fabric-covered frame around the window, with a functional shade tucked beneath it. “It’s a great fix when the interior architecture gets in the way of having the kind of window treatment you want,” she says.

TWOPAGES carries a wide range of shade materials—from linen blends and embroidered cottons to bamboo and woven wood—and offers every fold and lift type possible, so you can find the exact form and function to best fit your space.

Walsh likes to use drapery beyond traditional windows, especially if a room feels stark or echoey because of finishes such as marble, glass, or tile. A portière—a curtain hung in a doorway or cased opening—can create a sense of separation between spaces, soften an entryway, or help buffer cold air near an exterior door.

“Even if they’re purely decorative, drapery and window treatments absorb sound and provide texture and visual interest,” adds Kelly.

According to recent reports, the right fabric reinforces that effect. A lighter fabric like TWOPAGES Patti Belgian Flax Linen Curtain adds softness without feeling too heavy, while a drape with a more substantial texture, such as the brand’s Birkin Velvet Curtain, adds visual warmth and a richer feel, perfect for the colder months.

Sources indicate that the smallest details can make the biggest difference, even if custom treatments are not in your budget. Instead of a traditional curtain rod with finials on each end, which can look dated, Walsh advises using a French return rod, which is mounted on the wall and curves outward. This allows the end of the panels to sit flush against the wall while still creating space for a stack back.

It has been revealed that “A French return rod is by far the most elegant way to fake it and make your drapes look professional,” claims Walsh. But stay away from grommets—“they are a dead giveaway you did it yourself,” she says—and use rings with clips instead.

Head to twopagescurtains.com for more ideas.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that whether you’re curling up by the fire, hosting the family dinner, or bringing dessert to a Friendsgiving, a compliment-worthy manicure is a small comfort when the day gets chaotic. No matter what comes your way, at least your nails are done. And with all the passing, pouring, and photo-posing ahead, your hands are sure to get plenty of attention.

They’ll be passing the cranberry sauce, raising a glass for the toast, clutching a mug of cider—you name it. The good news is that fall offers one of the richest color palettes of the year. Think deep cranberry, burnished copper, mossy olive, and warm cinnamon, all shades that glow against autumn light and flatter nearly every skin tone.

And this season’s nail trends are as varied as the dishes on your table, from minimalist milky neutrals for the understated host to hand-painted leaves and shimmering gold flecks for the one who loves a little drama.

Ahead, check out some Thanksgiving nail ideas to inspire your next set.

You simply cannot go wrong with brown cat-eye nails. Whether you love a long almond silhouette or prefer a shorter, softer shape, this design feels rich, polished, and effortlessly autumnal.

Plaid nails in autumnal shades bring a fresh, playful spin to a fall manicure.

We love an ombré nail set, and this milky-to-espresso gradient fits right in with the season’s warm neutrals. The soft fade from creamy white to deep, coffee-bean brown feels cozy and sophisticated, like a latte in manicure form.

This butternut-squash yellow adds a fun pop of color to a darker fall palette.

According to recent reports, coffee-glazed nails are the manicure equivalent of a warm mug in your hands. It’s an easy pick for anyone who wants a little shimmer without going full metallic.

Can’t pick one fall shade? Wear them all, one on each finger. You’ll be surprised how well they work together.

Rich cherry red nails get a glam upgrade with a delicate gold cuticle line, a classic shade with a jewelry-box finish.

Deep, velvety, and effortlessly chic, this forest-inspired hue pairs beautifully with gold jewelry and cozy knits.

Brown nails with a white chrome topcoat melt into a frosty, taupe-y shade that’s simply stunning.

Rich, moody, and perfectly autumnal, this duo looks like a cranberry-and-herb tablescape on your fingertips.

Tortoiseshell nails are the chicest way to bring warm amber and espresso swirls to your Thanksgiving look.

Sheer, creamy, and effortlessly polished, this minimalist shade pairs with everything from cable-knit sweaters to your fanciest holiday dress.

Delicate, understated, and just a little whimsical, this look pairs a sheer neutral base with one or two hand-painted leaves and a dark French-tip manicure.

How a Connected Home Supports a Good Night’s Rest

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that as a certified holistic health coach and wellness content creator, Carolina Salazar knows the importance of a peaceful wind-down routine before bed.
  • Hubspace, The Home Depot’s exclusive smart home platform, powers more than 250 products across select private brands—like Hampton Bay, Husky, and Vissani—as well as national brand partners.
  • Some of the Hubspace app’s most practical features help users personalize lighting and improve home security.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that as a certified holistic health coach and wellness content creator, Carolina Salazar knows the importance of a peaceful wind-down routine before bed. She trusts Hubspace from The Home Depot that powers many of the smart devices in her home, to help ease her into a good night’s sleep.

Hubspace, The Home Depot’s exclusive smart home platform, powers more than 250 products across select private brands—like Hampton Bay, Husky, and Vissani—as well as national brand partners. It effortlessly connects everyday essentials, including smart security, indoor and outdoor lighting, appliances, switches, watering controls, and more.

Some of the Hubspace app’s most practical features help users personalize lighting and improve home security. Hubspace Connect, for example, lets you control compatible lighting from a single switch, while Vacation Mode is a security feature that turns lights and smart plugs on and off while you’re away. One of Salazar’s favorite features is Circadian Rhythm, which automatically transitions lights from cooler, whiter tones to warmer ones as the day goes on.

“I can set my lights to follow my circadian rhythm, so they shift automatically throughout the day,” claims Salazar. “And when they start to turn warm in the evening, that’s my cue to slow it down.” That can mean cozying up with a book, brewing a cup of hot tea, or, in her case, lighting a candle at her bedside and journaling. When Salazar is finished putting her thoughts to paper, she uses the Hubspace app to adjust the color, temperature, and brightness of her lights, dimming them as she gets closer to sleep. This can even be programmed automatically in order to reduce screen time before bed.

“Colder rooms bring better sleep, so I also have Hubspace turn on my AC at night,” she says.

Industry observers note that the Hubspace app is free to download and easily syncs with your home’s smart devices. You can enable voice control for screen-free commands—also a plus if you’re trying to reduce your pre-sleep screen time. And the app runs on both WiFi and Bluetooth—so even if the WiFi is down, your nighttime routine can still run seamlessly.

#112834. Tech Report: What to Watch After Finishing MobLand

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (806 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: What to Watch After Finishing MobLand

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (806 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • MobLand season 2 has come to an end.
  • It has been revealed that the obvious choice, if you haven't seen it already, is the other Guy Ritchie series.
  • Recent findings suggest that when an aristocratic army officer returns home after unexpectedly inheriting his family's estate instead of his older brother, he promptly discovers that it's at the heart of a notorious drug empire.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

MobLand season 2 has come to an end. (For now, at least—Tom Hardy and his motley crew have already started working on the third season.) Fortunately, there's an excellent selection of indicates on Netflix that'll fill that gory Guy Ritchie–crime thriller–shaped void in your weekend watchlist. Here's our pick of the five best ones that you should stream now that season 2 is over. And if you haven’t yet, make sure to read our breakdown of MobLand’s explosive season 2 finale—and that cliffhanger.

It has been revealed that the obvious choice, if you haven't seen it already, is the other Guy Ritchie series. The Gentlemen similarly revolves around a large mob family, has a lot of gore, and has the very same wicked sense of humor.

Recent findings suggest that when an aristocratic army officer returns home after unexpectedly inheriting his family's estate instead of his older brother, he promptly discovers that it's at the heart of a notorious drug empire. While he initially tries to shrug it off, he quickly becomes more involved in the criminal underworld than he imagined he would ... and it seems it comes more naturally to him than he'd have hoped.

The Gentlemen is twisty, wildly entertaining, and will be the closest you'll get to something that feels like MobLand, even though the shows are narratively quite different.

Dept. Q is another Netflix original that packs a punch – adapted from the Department Q novel series, it's a crazy crime thriller that only has one season so far, so is easy to catch up on (though a second is on the way).

After a top-rated detective returns to work from an attack that left his partner paralyzed and another policeman dead, he finds himself caught up in the investigation into a cold case that completely takes hold of him.

The plot, the sharp sarcastic writing and the way the whole show looks are enough to make Dept. Q an excellent watch, but it's the cast (led by an outstandingly complex performance from Matthew Goode) that makes this one particularly special.

It has been revealed that the spy thriller with the sharpest sense of humor, the most enthralling fight scenes—and, somehow amidst all the explosions—a whole lot of heart. It can be none other than Black Doves, Netflix's original espionage series that has swiftly become one of the streamer's best-loved highlights.

Industry observers note that helen Webb, a spy working for an organization called the Black Doves in an undercover marriage to a politician, has her position compromised, and mostly simple”'spy wife life” upended, when her lover is assassinated. In order to protect her and the secrecy of the Black Doves, her supervisor calls in an old friend to save her and sort out the mystery. However, the web of deceit proves unexpectedly complex and the three are soon in over their heads.

It has been revealed that other than being excellently acted (thanks to the legendary Keira Knightley, Ben Whishaw, Sarah Lancashire, and the supporting cast) and delightfully explosive, Black Doves is also surprisingly heartfelt, and you just can't help but root for its kooky cast. Even if they are all a bit nuts.

Once you're on board the Harlan Coben train, it's hard to hop off. I Will Find You, led by Sam Worthington and Severance's Britt Lower, is certainly one of the better adaptations of a Coben novel. Ridiculous, for sure, but undeniably entertaining the second you suspend your disbelief.

Five years after a man is wrongly imprisoned for the murder of his son, he receives information from his ex-wife's sister that his son might still be alive.

According to recent reports, if you've read the book (or seen enough Coben demonstrates that you know what's coming), then maybe you won't be quite as surprised by the twists and turns in this one. That being mentioned, it's breezy, easy-watching, and it's intensely bingeable if you're into that kind of thriller.

Aside from the sense of humor, the thing we all love most about Guy Ritchie's films and others in that realm is the stylised action sequences. If that's what you'll be missing when MobLand is over, then give Gangs of London a watch.

Sources indicate that based on the video game of the same name (but fortunately much better), the series revolves around the power struggles of rival gangs across London, all of which have different allegiances and international connections. When one young undercover police officer is tasked with infiltrating one of them to exploit a moment of weakness, things get ... very messy. Very fast.

It's perhaps not as funny (read: not at all comedic) as some of the other entries on this list, but it's classically gritty, gory British crime drama at its finest, and a must-see for fans of the genre.

Whether you equate The North Face with everyday city wear or outdoor adventures, it’s a solid, time-tested spot to get a gift for a loved one (or yourself). The brand has jackets and accessories with familiar winter looks, as well as products with less expected silhouettes that still offer protection from the elements in an understated style.

Here’s a look at some of the best cold-weather gear that will have you wrapping up the gift of warmth and durability… even if that gift is for yourself.

This is an easy gifting win because the warm, hooded, insulated jacket is a recognizable The North Face staple, evoking an unpretentious spin on the brand’s iconic Nuptse Jacket.

According to recent reports, it’s familiar, but it’s also practical—the kind of gift you feel good about because it’s going to get a ton of use. (And it can withstand the repeated wears.) The attached hood offers protection from biting winds, and the straightforward color options make it easy to pair with a variety of outfits, whether it’s something fun or part of a heavy bundling during the coldest days of winter. This is the perfect type of winter coat: warm but not too puffy.

The Zaneck Jacket is a great alternative to the Aconcagua, stepping away from the outdoorsy look the brand is best known for. It’s still waterproof and insulated, but it has a longer, more modern cut.

The Zaneck comes with a removable faux fur lining for the hood, which, in addition to being warm, means there are a couple of different looks that can be teased out of it. The straight cuffs add to its stylish feel in a way that doesn’t scream “I’m dressed for warmth and not fashion,” even though it’s doing both.

It has been revealed that the Lone Peak Triclimate 2 has a lot in common with the Zaneck. From a distance, they cut a similar silhouette. However, the Lone Peak adds a little versatility if you’re looking for a jacket that can handle a variety of climates.

It has been revealed that A removable, insulated inner jacket is attached to a removable, insulated top layer, which is fit for rainy conditions or as a spring or fall jacket. The insulated layer converts the whole thing into a winter-ready jacket. It also sports underarm vents capable of releasing heat in the middle of a long hike, ideal for outdoorsy types. The hood is removable and it’s got adjustable cuffs and an adjustable hem, making this a do-it-all jacket.

It might be easy to ignore the Pertex Jacket. It’s a bit unassuming. It doesn’t cut as stylish of a figure as the Zaneck, but it’s endlessly useful. The lightweight Pertex fabric will keep you dry in a downpour, but it also offers warmth without marshmallow-like bulk.

The lightweight aspect makes this the kind of coat you toss in the backseat on the way to a hike, just in case. It’s also great for layering, whether it’s tossed on over a sweater or layered under an overcoat to make a favorite jacket more winter-ready.

This edition of the classic Base Camp Duffel echoes the design details we love in The North Face’s jackets. While it’s got enough style and a heap of color options for daily use, it’s built for adventure.

It has been revealed that made with water- and tear-resistant fabric, it boasts 71 liters of storage space, a roomier option to the similar 31-liter version. Like all of the brand’s products, it’s built as if the designers have been through the rigors of outdoor adventures (and they probably have). It’s got a sweeping D-zip opening, backpack straps, mesh pockets, and compression straps in case you’re curious if you can pack 73 liters worth of gear into the 71-liter space. (You know you’ve tried.).

It has been revealed that the North Face has a lot of hats, none more iconic than this. The Salty Lined Beanie has a classic feel, fitting snuggly over the head with rib-knit texture, a cuffed shape, soft fabric, and ample color options to ensure it will match any jacket or accessory. The Salty Lined Beanie encapsulates the entire The North Face vibe in a small way: It’s stylish enough for a subway ride to work and practical enough for an outdoor adventure. Best of all, it’ll keep your ears warm in either instance.

In a recent development, often, the best glove is the one that disappears into the outfit. It looks seamless, keeping hands warm without drawing too much attention. The Etip Recycled Glove is about functionality first and foremost, but the simple design and understated colors makes it look good with a variety of winter outfits.

Sources indicate that while we all like to pretend we aren’t attached to our phones, the Etip makes a great modern gift because its stretchy fleece delivers a snug fit and the palms have touchscreen compatibility. That means you won’t have to take off your gloves to respond to that key text while the snow is falling.

The Holiday Party Etiquette Rules That Actually Matter, According to Lizzie Post

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Welcome to In Good Organization, where we ring in the festive season with fashion-insider entertaining tips, expert etiquette advice, and the perfect editor-approved hostess gifts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Welcome to In Good Organization, where we ring in the festive season with fashion-insider entertaining tips, expert etiquette advice, and the perfect editor-approved hostess gifts.

Holiday entertaining brings with it countless conundrums—from uninvited guests to the cousin who won’t put down their phone—for both hosts and guests. Agility is the key word; being able to elegantly pivot and respond to unexpected situations is what makes people feel comfortable and appreciated. Just in time for festive gatherings, ELLE spoke with Lizzie Post, author, co-president of the Emily Post Institute, and co-host of the Awesome Etiquette podcast, about all the things to keep in mind for a kind and gracious holiday. Read on for Post’s refreshingly down-to-earth tips.

No one can keep up with the incredible party décor shown on influencers’ posts, and you don’t have to try. Elegance can be found in any space, so host within the realities of your home. “You are not meant to be entertaining at the level of someone with a million-dollar budget and a gigantic home. You get to entertain at exactly your level, whatever that is,” Post notes. “All the little touches and the things you do to make people feel comfortable and welcome in your home are what make for a great host.”.

Bringing the wrong item can be an error on the part of the guest, but hosts should always make sure to minimize discomfort. “You want to take the etiquette high road and let it not be a problem. If [someone brings] an extra guest, rapidly enlist someone from your household or a trusted guest to help you zhuzh the arrangements in a discreet way so that the extra person does not feel like they were not meant to be there… [We have] the nearest-and-dearest to the host take smaller portions, so that everyone can have a decent portion.”.

It has been revealed that part of smartphone etiquette is letting others make their own choices. “You don’t overly control someone’s phone usage. Their rudeness will show on its own and will be noticed by more than just you… [Saying] ‘Could you make sure your phone is off, so you’re not tempted to use it throughout the evening?’ That is not a polite thing, even though it sounds gentle and so reasonable. That’s micromanagement.”.

In a recent development, bringing a thoughtful gift is always appreciated, but truly engaging with the event is what really matters. “There is no burden for hosting you. You’ve been invited and should feel welcome and like you belong in this space. You are not there to repay the efforts of the host. We are greeting our host. We are engaging with the other people. We are helping ourselves to the refreshments that are offered. If there are games or entertainment, we’re participating in that. If there’s a theme, we’ve showed up in the theme. That’s really how we’re a good guest.”.

Always say goodbye. “At the end of the night, say thank you and goodbye and seek out the host, whether it’s a substantial open house party or it’s a small dinner party to make that connection and express gratitude before we go.”.

Serving an item that a guest brought is at the host’s discretion. “A hostess gift is a hostess gift. It is not meant to be used that night with the people who brought it. It can be, but it does not have to be.”.

Sources indicate that whether you mail a card or not, make sure to share your appreciation with your host. “Thank-you notes are a wonderful idea and they allow you an extra level of expression, a little more thought. It doesn’t mean that a text message the next day would not also be appreciated. Any version of thanking your host after a party is a great version.”.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that christmas is just around the corner, and as the holiday spirit makes its way into our homes, it’s a good time to give your seasonal decor a refresh.
  • However, if you’re in the mood to try something a little different, here are seven trends on our radar for a chic Christmas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pictured above: A holiday-ready space by designer Marie Flanigan.

Sources indicate that christmas is just around the corner, and as the holiday spirit makes its way into our homes, it’s a good time to give your seasonal decor a refresh. This year, on-trend doesn’t have to mean brand-upcoming—designers love decorating with heirloom pieces collected over time.

However, if you’re in the mood to try something a little different, here are seven trends on our radar for a chic Christmas.

In a recent development, this winter, our decor is taking a note from European culture—again. Swedish folk art is emerging as a hot winter trend in both holiday and home decor. Defined by bold red hues, tulip motifs, and S-scrolls, the style blends cozy-core with the heritage style craze.

Industry observers note that “European folk influences are so big right now,” notes designer Johanna Lyle of Jo Lyle & Co. “Think Swedish Dala horses, quilt motifs, and decorative stitching. I think we will see those continue into holiday decor.”.

When it comes to her tree decor, interior designer Francesca Grace waves a hand at the carefully contrived, and she’s not alone. “My ornaments are collected from my travels, so the tree is really a collection of memories. I love unpacking them and remembering where each one came from. They don’t all match, and I wouldn’t want them to,” says Grace. “I let the ornaments lead. That mix feels much more personal to me, and it gives the tree something latest to say as the collection grows.” This year’s trends hinge on antiqued, inherited style, with one-off pieces that channel bold character and hardly ever come with a matching set.

Interior designer Marie Flanigan likes to add a fresh twist to her seasonal decor with dried oranges and pops of cranberry red.

Industry observers note that “We've seen such a beautiful resurgence of dried citrus in holiday decorating over the past few years,” Flanigan explains. “And I think cranberries are ready for their moment to shine. Their rich red hue feels especially festive, and I love the idea of incorporating them into fresh greenery, draping them across a mantel, or pairing them with dried oranges for a more layered look.”.

If there’s one classic Christmas element Grace hopes makes a comeback, it's multicolored lights. Inherently nostalgic, these bold-hued bulbs were a ’90s staple.

Sources indicate that “I’m ready for a little less restraint on the tree. Those reds, blues, greens, and yellows immediately bring back the feeling of Christmas as a child. They also pull together a collection of ornaments that might otherwise seem completely unrelated. White lights can be beautiful, but I want my Christmas tree to have some mischief,” indicates Grace.

Recent findings suggest that the classic red-and-green combination may take the title for the most iconic holiday palette, but this year, color trends are going complementary. While base colors stay warm and slightly rusted, patterned pieces are taking on cooler tones. This year, we’re also trading traditional plaid for Scottish tartan.

“Warm crimsons, rich browns, tactile fabrics, and blue-green plaids make a beautiful holiday palette,” states Elizabeth Bennett, cofounder of the interior design firm Kobel + Co.

It has been revealed that in a total rejection of mass-manufactured everything, handmade felt pieces are taking holiday homes by storm. The style has even coined a latest holiday aesthetic: #Kitschmas, and, according to Lyle, it’s here to stay. “As AI continues to homogenize design, things made by humans will feel more special and important. Handmade and crafted items create stories around decor that feel meaningful and can be treasured year after year,” she notes.

Moody browns are steadily emerging as the upcoming neutral as we inch closer to the new year, and lucky for our winter design schemes, the hue really is as versatile as it seems. Paired with powdery blues, bold crimsons, and even minty greens, chocolate brown grounds nearly any palette and matches every metallic hue.

“I’m particularly drawn to chocolate brown as an unexpected foundation for holiday color palettes. It's incredibly rich and versatile. I love the idea of moving beyond traditional red and green and allowing the existing colors of a room to inform the holiday decor. You can create something incredibly festive through tonal layering, subtle metallic accents, and variations in material,” Flanigan explains.

Industry News: Dreaming of Buying a Home Abroad? These 10 Countries Make It Shockingly Simple

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that over the last few years, many Americans have daydreamed about life abroad.
  • According to recent reports, certain countries, like Australia, Canada, and New Zealand, have bans on foreign buyers.
  • According to recent reports, choosing the right location can make moving abroad much less intimidating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that over the last few years, many Americans have daydreamed about life abroad. Moving internationally can often feel like a pipe dream, but with the right planning, it’s possible. However, lengthy visa processes, daunting language barriers, and a difficult-to-navigate legal system can make the dream feel more like a nightmare.

According to recent reports, certain countries, like Australia, Canada, and New Zealand, have bans on foreign buyers. Others, like Thailand, Cuba, and Vietnam, don’t allow outsiders to own property at all. On the other end of the spectrum are countries actively trying to attract foreign buyers, offering enviable incentives like affordable home prices, a smoother customs process, and an easier-to-navigate work-visa approval process.

According to recent reports, choosing the right location can make moving abroad much less intimidating. Ahead, we’re breaking down the ten best countries for Americans looking to buy property abroad. Whether you’re dreaming of relocating or searching for your perfect vacation home, these countries make buying as easy as possible and offer gorgeous landscapes too.

In a recent development, if you’ve ever dreamed of living among medieval architecture and rolling mountain ranges, Georgia might be the key to unlocking your fantasy. A bridge between Eastern Europe and Western Asia, the transcontinental country borders Russia, Turkey, Armenia, and the Black Sea, offering both subtropical and high-altitude climates. Thankfully, the real estate landscape is much less complex, with few legal or bureaucratic hurdles for American buyers, no residency or visa required (for up to a year), and remarkably fast processing times. In fact, the only major restriction in the Georgia market is that foreigners cannot purchase or own agricultural land, a nod to the importance of the local, small-scale farming cultures peppered across the country’s regions.

Recent findings suggest that uruguay’s buying process could not be more straightforward. South America’s second-smallest sovereign country requires no citizenship, visa, or prior approvals. Under Uruguayan law, foreign buyers are given the same rights as citizens and enjoy the benefits of free capital flow. Locals are just as, if not more, tourist-friendly. The country is known for its hospitality, laid-back café culture, and stunning coastal landscapes.

Instead of retiring to Florida, consider this balmy, beautiful Caribbean country—just a four-hour direct flight from the Fresh York area. Like everything else on the island, the real estate laws are relatively relaxed, making buying a house easy-breezy; and you can buy and own property without obtaining residency status or special permissions, as is the case in many other Caribbean islands. “Foreigners can own property outright in the Dominican Republic, with legal protections for foreign investors,” claims Mauricio Umansky, CEO and founder of The Agency. One important consideration is financing: You can certainly get a mortgage in the DR, but it may not be quite as cushy as what you can get in the U.S.—so pay cash if possible.

Great news if you’ve been wanting a more provincial life: Americans face zero restrictions when buying homes in France. The open market allows for statesiders to buy houses, apartments, or plots of land in the city, countryside, and coastal towns in person or remotely without needing citizenship, residency, or even a local visa. However, a purchase does not grant residency, so if you’re hoping to make France your permanent home, you’ll want to apply for a separate long-stay visa and note the Schengen 90-out-of-180-day rule. While buying may be simple, the finances are anything but. Closing fees, including notary fees, typically add seven to ten percent to your purchase. Mortgage rates are also incredibly hard to secure for U.S.-based buyers, thanks to strict debt-to-income caps and FATCA compliance. To simplify the process, many buyers opt to put 20 percent to 40 percent down in cash.

Perhaps the most American-friendly market, Panama boasts a large English-speaking market, virtually no restrictions on foreign property ownership, and uses the U.S. dollar as legal tender in a vastly affordable market. The Central American nation also offers residency programs like the Friendly Nations Visa, clearing the way legally for residency by investment. In addition to an efficient legal system and reliable market, Panama boasts breathtaking beaches, lush rainforests, and exceptional wildlife.

Industry observers note that if you’re hoping for a home in the coffee valleys of Colombia, you’ll need to hire a real estate lawyer before you start scouting for mountain chalets, coffee triangle treehouses, and rainforest retreats. The Caribbean country opts out of standardized agent licensing systems, making legal aid essential to verify title and freedom certificates. While citizenship isn’t required, you will need to secure a tourist visa and Colombian Tax ID to complete your purchase and register for property taxes.

In a recent development, the buying process in Greece is lengthy, though it is streamlined, with a clear checklist for American buyers to find success in the market. Hiring a local lawyer or notary is a great first step after scouting properties. Not only are they familiar with title checks and contracts, but they can also navigate the intricacies that come with buying in designated border areas or near military zones, which require special clearance for non–EU buyers. While the most popular areas for American buyers, like Athens and Crete, don’t come with heavy legal intricacies, buying any property in Greece will mean securing a Greek Tax Number—a small price to pay for cities with such rich histories and breathtaking seaside views.

The people in this popular Western European coastal country are famously friendly and inviting, and that extends to real estate. According to Samira Easton, a certified international property specialist with Premier Sotheby’s International Realty, Portugal offers a Golden Visa Program, which makes it simple to buy property and gain residency; clear real estate laws; and a well-established network of English-speaking real estate agents, lawyers, and notaries to help you during the process.

In a recent development, belize is home to one of the most vibrant, tourist-friendly cultures in Central America, mixing Mayan, Hispanic, Asian, and Creole cultures in its dense rainforests and rolling low plains. Buying here is as easy as it can get, as outright ownership applies to foreigners, and a British-inspired legal system abolishes language barriers and makes contracts easier to understand. Even more, there is no capital gains tax in Belize, and property taxes trend low. The country also boasts vibrant marine life and is home to the world’s second-largest barrier reef.

It has been revealed that spain may have ended its investor visa program in 2025, but the real estate market is still remarkably easy for Americans to navigate. The country right now imposes no restrictions on foreign or nonresident property ownership, but there are a few things you’ll need to procure before you buy, like a Foreigner Identification Number, which is mandatory for taxes. Despite the minor hurdles, the market is booming both on the ground and online. “There are also numerous online resources and property portals available, so it’s easy to find listings and information,” Easton says. This is a boon for those who aren’t able to make the trip over to Europe to house shop in person.Note that buying property does not grant you residency or bypass the country’s 90-day Schengen limit. If you’re hoping to turn your Spanish holiday into your everyday, you’ll have to apply for a separate visa.
