📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve been writing gift guides as a shopping editor for years. Usually, I’m very sentimental, wanting to recommend thoughtful gifts to make your loved ones smile. But all bets are off when it comes to White Elephant gifts. I want to cause chaos at your family gift swap. Your gift should be the one everyone fights over.

If you're not sure what a White Elephant exchange is or how it works, just know this: it's really fun, and it's one of the only times when stealing is not only totally acceptable, but encouraged. Basically, it's a blind gift exchange that, when the recipient reveals the gift they chose, they can keep it or put it back and steal someone else's gift. It's a cheeky little game that is a great way to get into the holiday spirit.

It’s also a really affordable way to exchange gifts as a big group. No worries about finding the perfect thing for someone specific. Just bring something cool enough for anybody to enjoy, and there’s usually a budget cap. So for this guide, I provided the best white elephant gifts under $50. They’re so budget-friendly and unique that you might want to do all of your gift shopping below, or buy some items of your own. Worry not; we won’t judge.

Additional copy by Jessica Cherner.

This is the ultimate tool for any candle lover. In just one sleek, swan-shaped package, it’s a candle snuffer, wick dipper, trimmer, and wax spoon. It comes in gold or raven black, and it’ll be perfect coffee table decor.

It has been revealed that time to level up that holiday hot cocoa. This spice kit comes with the classic velvety cocoa mix, in addition to sustainably harvested Guntur Sannam chili and fragrant cardamom pods. Your hot chocolate can be as complex as your morning cup of chai.

No city-dweller will say no to extra storage. It’s especially helpful when it comes in a cute and colorful package, like these cache boxes. Use it to hide junk mail, Q-tips, or any other tiny clutter.

The plant lover in your life will jump at the chance to steal this care essential. The GOHA Leaf Sweep is Associate Shopping Editor Janae McKenzie’s secret to a shiny, eye-catching houseplant collection. “I use it to clean my plant’s broad leaves, especially the tall ones out of reach,” McKenzie notes. “It prevents dirt buildup and keeps pests at bay.” We even have a special code for HB readers to save 10% on this handy tool: use HB10 at checkout.

Sources indicate that yes, they might own a wine opener already, but we doubt it’s as cute as this corkscrew. The color-blocked bow tie shape makes opening the next bottle look even more fun. A bar cart isn’t complete without it.

In a recent development, speaking of drinks, does their coaster set actually soak up the water? Or does it just pool on top to make a mess later? They can protect their furniture in style with this coaster set made from acrylic yarn. Did we mention they’re machine-washable?

A lull in conversation is a thing of the past with this beautiful set of question cards. Inspired by creative power couple Suleika Jaouad & Jon Batiste, this deck turns the chatter from “What do you do for work?” to something more insightful and engaging.

According to recent reports, if you love pickles, you’ll understand why this one won’t last long in the White Elephant pile. No more digging into the jar to grab the perfect spear. This mini-fork makes every charcuterie board way easier to assemble.

The commuters in the room might argue over this one. Anyone who meal-preps will love this portable food warmer. Keep your lunch nice and toasty, whether you have a microwave within reach or not. Plus, it’s spill-proof and dishwasher-safe.

This is a wake-up call in a box. It’s the ideal luxury soap for post-workout showers or mornings that need a little extra invigoration. Peppermint wakes up the senses, and poppy seeds and sea salt exfoliate the skin for an extra-fresh layer.

Recent findings suggest that every kitchen needs a great spoon rest, and who could say no to this adorable silicone crab? This pot-side helper makes every complicated recipe feel extra fun to put together.

According to recent reports, these tinned fish tongs make the most delicate seafood easy to serve and snack on. They were designed by and for the professional chefs of the world. They’re made from stainless steel like plating tweezers, but as easy to use as takeout chopsticks.

Sources indicate that we all have days that feel extra difficult to deal with. And this deck of affirmations is tongue-in-cheek, but motivational enough to get through it. “I keep this on my desk for the longest workdays,” McKenzie says. “100 little reassurances to make me laugh.”.

In a recent development, why not take a creative, analog hobby on the go? This is a travel-friendly watercolor painting kit with a built-in wooden palette and a refillable water brush. So no messy water cup is needed, and the sketchbook comes attached.

Instead of fresh-cut flowers that’ll die in a few days, go with this mini grow kit for long-blooming, celebratory dahlias. The colorful flowers grow in a hydroponic system, so water goes right to the roots, and it’s easy to take care of.

In a recent development, picture wispy incense smoke coming from the chimney of this adorable English cottage. The ceramic holder comes with 20 woody incense cones. If cottagecore isn’t your style, there’s a Nordic cabin, an Adobe house, and a Parisian townhouse to choose from.

Get the luxury of Soho Home’s members-only style for under $50 with these chic resin salad servers. They’re inspired by the flagship London location, and they have an iridescent finish that’s perfect for the next dinner party.

Hand-pressed rainbow glass makes for quite the attractive bathroom countertop piece. Use it to hold your soap, cotton rounds, supplements or any other morning essentials.

Packing cubes makes any frequent traveler feel a bit more organized, and Rifle Paper Co. designed them as stylish as the clothes inside. The set includes three zippered packing cubes of different sizes and a matching drawstring laundry bag, all in a metallic floral finish.

Lea Michele Wants a Scream Queens Reboot, Too

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1642 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor.
  • Industry observers note that with multiple projects on the horizon, all eyes are on Lea Michele.
  • Industry observers note that it’s a natural collaboration, as the Bronx-born Michele is the perfect shepherd for a curated NYC experience.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Industry observers note that with multiple projects on the horizon, all eyes are on Lea Michele. Glee is getting a reboot; fans are begging for Scream Queens to come back, and the actress and singer is about to embark on a tour with Chess co-star Aaron Tveit. She also just starred in Kiehl’s fresh “Gift Like a Local” campaign. In partnership with Uber, Michele traveled around to small businesses in New York City and doled out Kiehl’s products. The Glee star even picked most of the stops herself. “Kiehl’s had emailed me and they said, ‘We really want to feature some local businesses in this campaign. Can you send us some of your thoughts?’” she states. “It took me about 30 seconds. I had an email with 50 places.”.

Industry observers note that it’s a natural collaboration, as the Bronx-born Michele is the perfect shepherd for a curated NYC experience. In many ways, she breathes Newly introduced York. She’s starred on Broadway multiple times, most recently in Chess, which just received a Grammy nomination for Best Musical Theater Album. In the later seasons of Glee, her character, Rachel Berry, moved to New York to chase her Broadway dreams (Michele is also rumored to be returning to the show’s reboot). She at the moment lives in New York with her husband and two children. On the morning of our interview, fresh off a sold-out show with Tveit at the Beacon Theater, she’s having a classic New York morning. “I took my kids to school. I was walking in the sunshine, I had my matcha. I’m getting ready for an event right now,” she notes. “It just is a great day.”.

Below, Michele talks about Glee, her collaboration with Kiehl’s, and whether she’d ever come back for a Scream Queens reboot.

It has been revealed that aaron [Tveit] would love my personal favorite, the Grapefruit Body Cleanser. That’s just my tried-and-true. I used it this morning. If you’re feeling a little tired, it helps you to wake up and feel good. But even if you’re not, if you’re feeling like how I felt this morning, energized and happy, it’s just one of my favorite ways to start the day. Love, love, love their body lotion. It’s one of the only body lotions that I feel like actually works for me and helps to really moisturize my skin. They have all these amazing little kits as well over the holidays. I’ve given my dad Kiehl’s lip balm and eye cream in his stockings every year for the holidays.

Sources indicate that I’m really excited to be a part of the Kiehl’s family now. I love our commercial that we shot and the fact that we had the opportunity to support some of the local small businesses.

According to recent reports, I grew up here. I was born in the Bronx. My father owned a deli here in the city. We had ice cream parlors and candy shops. We featured Élan Flowers in my neighborhood. Seasons in Times Square is somewhere that I go all the time and buy flowers for people in Broadway demonstrates. I love Onda, it’s an amazing little facial and wellness store in Tribeca. Obviously, so many little coffee shops. I mean, the list is quite long.

I just love everything white. I love all-white. My house is all white, but peonies are my favorite flowers. I love hydrangeas. I love white roses. I just love a big white bouquet of flowers.

According to recent reports, [Aaron Tveit] and I just found out this morning that almost the entire tour sold out. [It] took less than 24 hours. At our show last night, I think we learned so much about what the show is and what the show could be. We had to cut 10 songs from the concert because we just have so much material. I don’t think that we’re going to do the same show every night. I think that each city is going to get their own show. We’re going to do some of what I would say are our greatest hits together, and some of our individual hits that I think that I will always do in concert, but I really just feel like there’s so much that we can do.

I want Radio City to be epic. We haven’t really talked about having some friends join us, but that’s also something that we could definitely do if we wanted to and bring out some friends to sing some songs with us. The options are endless.

Recent findings suggest that [Aaron is] one of my dearest friends. His wife is one of my closest friends. He’s friends with my husband. Our children are friends. [It’s] amazing that I get to work with someone that I just respect and care about so much.

Industry observers note that it feels awesome. Normally I know when these things are happening, but my publicist texted me in the morning. She was like, “You got a Grammy nomination.” I cried. My reaction was so, even for me, surprising and unexpected. I just broke down. My husband was walking our kids out the door to take them to school, and I was like, “I can’t believe this. We got nominated for a Grammy.” It means so much. I can’t tell you the talent of the cast of Chess. Every single cast member, the most extraordinary talent, our ensemble, the band. To have the cast get this incredible honor, it’s beyond well deserved. I think every single person who saw Chess would agree.

Sources indicate that we are constantly one-upping each other in the wellness world. He’ll be like, “Have you seen this? Do you have this?” He had some sort of, I don’t know if it was an infrared mat, and I was like, “Okay, I need that. What’s that?” He saw that I had an amazing water filter in my house, and he’s like, “Okay, what’s that? I need that.” He is probably one of the only people who could rival me in my biohacking, wellness, and taking care of myself.

Most of the time during Chess, if we weren’t talking about Summer House and all of the drama, we were talking about what are all of the wellness things that we’re doing and to try to stay healthy.

Industry observers note that I’ve been doing Pilates for years. Emma Roberts took me to my first Pilates class when we were living in Upcoming Orleans together, shooting Scream Queens. We went to Romney Studios and did a private lesson. I fell in love with it. Since then, I’ve done mat Pilates and hot Pilates and power Pilates. Everything. I felt pretty good going into this, being like, “I know what I need to know.”.

It wasn’t my first time playing a killer on television, which was also kind of funny. It was so awesome to return to television last night after so many years, and I just had a really great time.

I met a little girl last night at the meet-and-greet. She was probably 7 years old, and she came to see the concert with her two dads. Her dads were like, “We just are starting to show her some of the musical numbers.” I was like, “Look at you, you’re a little Rachel Berry.” She had her headband on and her cute little penny loafers, and it was just the sweetest thing. What we all created, and what Ryan and Brad and Ian created with Glee, was just so amazing. The things that people say to me about how much it affected their life and brought them so much joy means the world to me.

I hear stories like that from people all the time, and I know that it really means so much to all of us.

In a recent development, the love for Scream Queens has always been there. Emma [Roberts] and I love that show. We talk about it all the time. Ryan knows, too. Ryan and I talk about it always and I beg him all the time. I’m like, “Can we please bring Scream Queens back?” Ryan should do it. It would be awesome.

According to recent reports, it’s so beautiful. I talked a lot about Spring Awakening during my concert last night. We are celebrating 20 years of Spring Awakening opening on Broadway this December. We have a group chat with the original cast. Myself, Lauren Pritchard, and Jonathan Groff are planning a really special private night just for the original cast, a little celebration. I’m so excited that it’s coming to Off-Broadway. My dear, dear, dear sister, Lilli Cooper, is going to be in it. Spring Awakening is such a beautiful and important show, and so anytime that it has the opportunity for people to see it, it should be there. It’s the most beautiful piece of art.

Industry observers note that oh, yeah. I’ve had the opportunity and the real honor to be a part of some incredible original Broadway productions, both with Ragtime and Spring Awakening. It’s an incredible, incredible show.

In a recent development, there are so many. I want to do everything, I really do. I want to do it all. If I am lucky enough to perform on Broadway for the rest of my life, then that would just be the greatest dream. There are so many great highlights that have been on Broadway that could be revived and amazing pieces and incredibly talented artists that are writing original pieces as well. So, I’m ready and available for whatever is to come.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.
